Dear Dr. Morrison,

Thank you for seeing Leo Davies, a 5-year-old boy referred to your service for a comprehensive cardiovascular assessment. 

Leo was born at term without perinatal complications. He has a known non-conductive auditory deficit present since the neonatal period, having failed his newborn hearing screening and subsequently receiving a diagnosis of profound bilateral inner-ear deafness. He has adapted well to bilateral cochlear processors and is meeting all of his motor developmental milestones, currently attending a local kindergarten. 

During a recent pre-operative workup for routine adenoid evaluation, an incidental 12-lead electrocardiogram demonstrated a significantly lengthened ventricular repolarization phase, with a calculated corrected QT duration measuring approximately 515 ms across several leads. In addition, his rhythm strip revealed a sluggish resting pulse for his age, characterized by baseline sinus rates consistently lingering between 52 and 58 beats per minute.

On physical examination today, he is well-nourished and active. Auscultation revealed clear lung fields bilaterally and crisp heart sounds without any audible murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Peripheral perfusion is brisk, femoral pulses are robust, and his abdomen is soft and non-tender. There is no family history of unexplained syncopal episodes or early cardiac events. He takes no routine prescription medications.

Given these electrical findings alongside his longstanding sensory deficit, I would appreciate your expert assessment regarding his conduction properties and your guidance on appropriate long-term management.

Sincerely,

Dr. Arthur Pendelton
Oakridge Pediatric Clinic
